issues.legal_issue: An appeal concerning proceedings pending in a court at the time of territorial reorganisation lies to the court that would have appellate jurisdiction over that court under the post-reorganisation arrangement.
material_facts: Applications seeking restoration of properties under a decree were pending before a subordinate court when territorial changes took effect.
The appeal was filed after those changes, and some of the properties covered by the decree were then in a different territory.
issues.conclusion: The appeal to the Calcutta High Court was competent because that court had appellate jurisdiction over the subordinate court under the hypothetical arrangement prescribed for proceedings instituted after the appointed day.
issues.legal_principle: Paragraph 4(2) of the Indian Independence (Legal Proceedings) Order, 1947, directs that an appeal concerning proceedings pending in a court shall lie to the court that would have appellate jurisdiction over it if the proceedings were instituted there after the appointed day. The words do not mean that the proceedings must actually have been capable of institution there after that day. The Court followed Tirlok Nath v. Moti Ram, A.I.R. 1950 East Punjab 149.

predicates.proceedings_were_pending_at_territorial_: Proceedings were pending before a court when territorial reorganisation took effect.
predicates.appeal_concerns_those_proceedings: A party appealed in relation to those pending proceedings.

issues.definition: When proceedings were pending at territorial reorganisation and an appeal concerns them, the appeal lies to the appellate forum assigned to the court under the post-reorganisation arrangement.

issues.legal_issue: Applications that are in substance applications to execute a decree are execution applications, and orders made on them are appealable.
material_facts: The decree permitted the decree-holders to seek restoration of properties if the judgment-debtors defaulted.
The decree-holders applied to the court for restoration following alleged defaults.
The applications were not framed in the proper form but sought enforcement of the decree.
issues.conclusion: The applications were in substance applications for execution of the new decree, and orders made on them were appealable; the High Court’s reasoning that they were applications in the suit producing appealable decrees under the Code of Civil Procedure was not accepted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the applications according to their substance as applications for execution of the decree passed under section 36 of the Bengal Money Lenders Act, 1940. Orders on applications for execution are appealable. The Court rejected the view that these were suit applications whose orders were decrees within section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

predicates.proceeding_is_an_appeal_from_an_order: A party brings an appeal against an order made on an application.
predicates.application_substantially_seeks_executio: The application, whatever its form, seeks enforcement of a decree.

issues.definition: An appeal from an order is available when the underlying application, in substance, seeks execution of a decree.

issues.legal_issue: A court hearing an appeal from an execution order may determine whether a default occurred and uphold restoration required by the decree, without the executing court going behind the decree.
material_facts: The decree provided for restoration of the properties to the decree-holders upon default in payment obligations imposed on the judgment-debtors.
The decree-holders applied for restoration, alleging default in an instalment and in payment of revenue and cesses.
The Supreme Court found that defaults had occurred in the instalment and in revenue and cess payments.
The High Court allowed the appeal and ordered restoration, reversing the subordinate court’s rejection of the applications.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to determine that the judgment-debtors had defaulted and that the decree-holders were entitled to restoration; the contention that no default occurred could not be sustained.
issues.legal_principle: An executing court cannot go behind the decree. Where the decree makes restoration conditional on default and the record establishes the specified defaults, the court may enforce the decree accordingly. The applications were treated as execution applications, rather than as suit applications resulting in decrees under section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

predicates.proceeding_is_an_appeal_from_an_executio: The proceeding is an appeal from an order on an application to execute a decree.
predicates.decree_makes_restoration_conditional_on_: The decree provides for restoration if the judgment-debtor defaults on an obligation it imposes.
predicates.default_occurred: The judgment-debtor failed to meet an obligation that triggers restoration under the decree.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an execution order, the decree makes restoration conditional on default, and that default occurred, the decree-holder is entitled to restoration under the decree.

issues.legal_issue: The location of properties in a different territory does not prevent the appellate court from deciding entitlement to restoration when it has jurisdiction over the appeal.
material_facts: The appeal concerned restoration of properties, most of which were situated outside the territory of the appellate court after territorial reorganisation.
The proceedings seeking restoration had been pending in the subordinate court before the territorial changes.
The appellate court considered whether the judgment-debtors had defaulted under the decree.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had jurisdiction to decide whether default occurred and to make the necessary order for restoration; whether possession of properties in the other territory could in fact be obtained was a separate matter and did not prevent that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Under paragraph 4(2) of the Indian Independence (Legal Proceedings) Order, 1947, the appellate forum for proceedings pending at territorial reorganisation is determined by treating the lower court as the court in which the proceedings could and should have been instituted after the appointed day. The practical ability to obtain possession of property in another territory is not part of the appellate court’s inquiry into entitlement to restoration.

predicates.proceeding_is_an_appeal_about_restoratio: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an order for restoration of property.
predicates.underlying_proceedings_were_pending_at_t: The proceedings underlying the appeal were pending in a court when territorial reorganisation took effect.
predicates.property_is_outside_appellate_territory: The property whose restoration is sought is situated outside the appellate court’s territory.

issues.definition: When an appeal about restoration arises from proceedings pending at territorial reorganisation, the appellate court may decide entitlement to restoration even if the property is outside its territory.
